---
title: "Lab 05 — Estimation, uncertainty, and hypothesis testing"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
star <- read_csv("data/STAR.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(classtype = factor(
    classtype,
    labels = c("Small class", "Regular class", "Regular class with aide")
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(g4reading), classtype %in% c("Small class", "Regular class"))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab05", title = "Estimation and hypothesis testing")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "A 95 percent confidence interval means…",
  q2 = "A p-value is…",
  q3 = "Small class versus regular class, fourth-grade reading…",
  q4 = "A small, imprecise difference can fail to reject and still leave the policy question open. Say why, using this comparison."
)
```

## What you will do

Read an interval and a test as uncertainty about the STAR reading gap, not as proof of a policy. Download the `.txt`.

```{r test-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=3}
t.test(g4reading ~ classtype, data = star)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("In repeated samples, 95 percent of such intervals would cover the true difference.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The probability that this interval contains the true difference is 95 percent."),
  answer("The effect is large because the interval is a confidence interval."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("The probability of a gap at least this large if the two means were equal.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The probability that the null hypothesis is true."),
  answer("The size of the effect."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("The small-class mean is only a few points higher, and the 95 percent interval includes zero.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Small classes score about 30 points higher, and the interval excludes zero."),
  answer("The means match exactly, so randomization failed."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Estimate, interval, and what failing to reject does not prove.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
